transcript:
This message comes from Schwab. At Schwab, you can get everything from self-directed investing to full-service wealth management all in one place.
No matter your investing goal, life stage, amount to invest, or know-how, you can invest your way with Schwab.
Live from NPR News, I'm Giles Snyder. Attorneys for Tennessee death row inmate Krista Pike say Pike is still alive but in critical condition.
They spoke to reporters Thursday after the state's failed attempt to execute Pike by lethal injection for a 1995 murder when she was 18.
From member station WPLN, Mariana Bacchial reports on Tennessee Republican Governor Bill Lee's call for a third-party review of what went wrong.
This marks the second time Governor Bill Lee has issued a moratorium to review the state's execution protocols.
A 2022 review found that the drugs used had not been properly inspected, leading to an overhaul of the system and a new lethal injection process.
This is a process that has been used over 100 times in this country without this outcome.
Lee is term limited and will likely not be governor when the investigation is complete. The front-runner for the governorship, U.S. Senator Marsha Blackburn, has called for the state to "bring back the electric chair."
For NPR News, I'm Mariana Bacchial in Nashville.
Cornell University students are calling on school officials to answer questions on how they handled the initial report of a gang rape at a fraternity house in 2024.
Felix Reichman-Kernau is a Cornell freshman.
Just being more transparent to the students is necessary. We've been sent a couple emails, but they've not been very clear with what actions are being taken, if any, or how the university is cooperating with local and state police on this specific investigation.
New York Governor Kathy Hochul has appointed state Attorney General Letitia James as a special prosecutor in the case in a statement. Hochul said she has lost faith in the local district attorney.
Oklahoma President Trump repeated his promise to give Americans $5,000 if Republicans win the House and Senate.
And here's Franco Ordonez reports on Trump's campaign kickoff for next month's midterm elections.
The president kicked off a campaign sprint where he promised to visit Republicans in 35 of the most competitive races across the country.
But he stopped first in Oklahoma to workshop some campaign lines and thanked the red state for its ongoing support.
Trump got one of his biggest ovations when he again promised to give each American adult a check for $5,000 if Republicans maintain control of Congress.
The extraordinary pledge has raised eyebrows among both Republicans and Democrats.
Some Democrats liken the offer to a bribe.
Trump claimed Republicans would be able to make the payments through revenue generated by tariffs and other economic policies.
Though analysts say the tariff revenue would not be enough. Franco Ordonez, NPR News, Duran, Oklahoma.
Before heading to Oklahoma, President Trump delivered a nearly hour-long speech at a Peterbilt truck factory in Denton, Texas. This is NPR.
Rescue teams in Southern California are looking for a fifth person who remains missing following the crash of a medical helicopter Wednesday off California's Catalina Island.
The Coast Guard says the helicopter was transporting a patient off the island when it went down shortly after takeoff. Two people were killed and two others hospitalized.
Google put a satellite in orbit Thursday that it hopes can pave the way for orbiting AI data centers. And Pierre-John Ruach has more.
The device is about the size of a refrigerator, and on board it has four microchips designed by Google that are already in data centers on Earth.
The satellite is part of a research project at Google called Suncatcher because the big lure of putting data centers in space is the nearly unlimited supply of free energy from the sun.
Google plans to run AI workloads through the chips, testing how they perform after the stresses of launch and while being hit by space radiation.
They'll also gauge how hot the chips get and how well they can be cooled by radiator panels without wind or water to help.
The eventual goal is to launch constellations of similar satellites that will process AI workloads, communicate by laser link and function as flying data centers in space.
And a note, Google is a financial supporter of NPR. John Ruach, NPR News.
A quick flight to the International Space Station. Four astronauts have arrived at the orbiting outposts following an eight-hour flight.
The fastest journey to the station for not only SpaceX but any other U.S. entity, including NASA.
The four include Commander Jessica Watkins, the first black woman to lead a crew to orbit. They are to spend six months aboard the station.
I'm Giles Snyder, NPR News.
